claims.text: The starting Mg-Al-Cr-Ni powder mixture has elemental segregation, an unstable microstructure, and susceptibility to eutectic formation and porosity.
Holding the alloy at 850 °C for 2 hours will stabilize the matrix, suppress eutectic segregation, and prevent volatile loss.
A subsequent 920 °C anneal for 30 minutes will trigger dynamic recrystallization.
A subsequent 920 °C anneal for 30 minutes will promote L12 ordering without reaching the volatility threshold.
Hot pressing at 50 MPa enhances densification at lower sintering temperatures.
The two-stage treatment will form a fine-grained FCC-L12 composite microstructure.
A fine-grained FCC-L12 microstructure acts as an oxidation barrier and suppresses detrimental eutectic or Laves phases.
Temperatures above approximately 900 K can rapidly increase lattice disorder, decrease dislocation density, and degrade mechanical properties.
The 850 °C stage avoids the lattice disorder and dislocation-density decrease associated with temperatures above 900 K.
Standard homogenization can leave eutectic formations and undissolved Heusler phase in an Hf-containing Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti alloy.
Dynamic recrystallization can refine grains and promote a BCC/B2-to-FCC transformation that contributes to oxidation resistance.
L12 ordering creates high-energy interfaces that inhibit outward diffusion of volatile elements and produce a protective surface layer.
The proposed two-stage treatment will achieve greater than 98% relative density.
The proposed two-stage treatment will reduce oxidation rates relative to isothermal sintering at 950 °C.
The proposed two-stage treatment will improve mechanical stability relative to isothermal sintering at 950 °C.
Isothermal sintering at 950 °C typically results in significant porosity in the proposed Mg-Al-Cr-Ni alloy.
Isothermal sintering at 950 °C causes eutectic segregation and potential Mg volatility.
Below 800 °C, suppressed atomic diffusion causes porosity above 5%.
Above 1000 °C, volatility and phase instability occur, including gap formation in oxide layers.
The reversibility of L12-related ordering observed in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 may not transfer to Mg-based alloys lacking similar local chemical-order and phase-boundary dynamics.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says the 850 °C stage avoids behavior occurring above 900 K, but 850 °C is approximately 1123 K; the subsequent 920 °C stage is approximately 1193 K. Both proposed stages are above the stated 900 K boundary.
The intervention confidently states that 920 °C remains below the volatility threshold, while the uncertainty field says the Mg volatility threshold within 800–1000 °C is not quantified.
